title: Spring constant calculation
description: Essential: Correctly calculates spring constant k = 400 N/m using Hooke's law and equilibrium condition at constant velocity.

title: Friction at constant velocity
description: Important: Recognizes that at constant velocity, spring force equals kinetic friction force (μmg = 18 N).

title: Compressed spring friction (6cm)
description: Essential: Correctly determines frictional force magnitude = 16 N when spring is compressed to 6 cm.

title: Static friction application
description: Important: For compression to 6 cm, identifies that spring force (16 N) is less than maximum static friction, so friction equals spring force.

title: Compressed spring friction (16cm)
description: Essential: Correctly determines frictional force magnitude = 18 N when spring is compressed to 16 cm.

title: Kinetic friction application
description: Important: For compression to 16 cm, recognizes spring force (24 N) exceeds maximum static friction, so kinetic friction (18 N) acts.

title: Direction specification
description: Optional: Includes correct directions for friction forces (right for 6 cm, left for 16 cm).

title: Hooke's law misapplication
description: Pitfall: Uses wrong sign in Hooke's law (e.g., F = k|x| without considering compression vs. stretch).

title: Friction type confusion
description: Pitfall: Treats all cases as kinetic friction or fails to compare spring force to maximum static friction.
